summary.title: Cybersecurity News Briefing: Critical Vulnerabilities and Supply-Chain Threats

overview.executive_summary: The most consequential developments include active exploitation of PHP and Plex vulnerabilities, critical GitLab and Node.js flaws, software supply-chain compromises, exposed customer secrets, and large-scale ransomware and cybercrime activity. Organizations should prioritize urgent patching, credential rotation, incident investigation, and review of affected software and infrastructure.

sections.heading: PHP2Shell vulnerabilities
sections.what_happened: CISA urged immediate patching for two critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution vulnerabilities in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Fixed versions include PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35.
sections.why_it_matters: The flaws affect PHP installations serving web requests, and an exploit attempt was detected before public disclosure.
sections.recommended_attention: Inventory PHP systems and immediately patch internet-facing installations. Take unsupported versions offline if they cannot be updated.

sections.heading: Plex2Shell exploitation
sections.what_happened: CISA warned that attackers are actively exploiting four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server, collectively called Plex2Shell, to breach servers.
sections.why_it_matters: The vulnerabilities have entered active exploitation and can expose Plex server environments.
sections.recommended_attention: Check Plex deployments for affected versions, apply available fixes, and investigate suspicious server activity.

sections.heading: Critical GitLab code execution flaw
sections.what_happened: GitLab released fixes for a maximum-severity flaw allowing unauthenticated remote code execution on self-managed servers. The issue affects releases dating back to version 7.0 in 2014.
sections.why_it_matters: The vulnerability spans roughly 12 years of releases and may affect systems patched by an earlier update.
sections.recommended_attention: Verify the exact fixed version for every self-managed GitLab instance and patch immediately.

sections.heading: LiteLLM supply-chain compromise
sections.what_happened: Attackers compromised LiteLLM release controls and published version 1.107.0 through PyPI and Docker Hub with a credential stealer and backdoor.
sections.why_it_matters: The incident could expose developer credentials and systems that consumed the compromised package or image.
sections.recommended_attention: Identify use of LiteLLM 1.107.0, quarantine affected systems, rotate exposed credentials, and review build and deployment activity.

sections.heading: Railway customer secrets exposure
sections.what_happened: Railway disclosed anomalous activity involving systems storing customer environment variables. An unauthorized party may have accessed encrypted variables and, in some cases, decrypted contents.
sections.why_it_matters: Environment variables can contain credentials and other secrets used by applications and infrastructure.
sections.recommended_attention: Rotate potentially exposed credentials and review access to Railway environments.

sections.heading: Node.js Brotli remote code execution flaw
sections.what_happened: Node.js security updates for supported 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x release lines fixed 10 flaws, including a Brotli decompression bug that could allow remote code execution.
sections.why_it_matters: The issue affects all supported Node.js release lines and could let attackers run code on affected systems.
sections.recommended_attention: Update each supported Node.js deployment to its fixed release and assess exposed services.

sections.heading: HTTP/3 QPACK denial-of-service flaws
sections.what_happened: Researchers disclosed flaws allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash many HTTP/3 servers and trigger memory amplification of up to 4,000-fold. Working proof-of-concept code was released.
sections.why_it_matters: A small amount of malicious traffic could create severe memory pressure or service disruption.
sections.recommended_attention: Assess HTTP/3 exposure, apply vendor mitigations when available, and monitor memory and availability anomalies.

sections.heading: Onamae Desktop Cloud compromise
sections.what_happened: Attackers compromised Japan's Onamae Desktop Cloud infrastructure and installed malware on as many as 26,739 customer servers.
sections.why_it_matters: A provider-level compromise can affect a large number of downstream hosted systems simultaneously.
sections.recommended_attention: Customers should investigate hosted servers for malware, review provider communications, and rotate credentials where appropriate.

sections.heading: SafePay ransomware campaign
sections.what_happened: CISA said the SafePay ransomware group has breached more than 600 critical-infrastructure organizations worldwide since 2024.
sections.why_it_matters: The scale and focus on critical infrastructure indicate sustained risk to essential services and operators.
sections.recommended_attention: Review ransomware defenses, privileged access, incident-response readiness, and critical-system backups.

sections.heading: eMudhra certificate authority compromise
sections.what_happened: Eight eMudhra intermediate certificate private keys were compromised after researchers found they were weak enough to recover almost instantly. Mozilla, Google, and Apple blocked the certificates.
sections.why_it_matters: Compromised intermediate certificate keys could be used to forge trusted certificates for legitimate websites.
sections.recommended_attention: Confirm browser and trust-store protections are current and investigate certificate validation or interception anomalies.

sections.heading: ConnectWise supply-chain attack using AI agents
sections.what_happened: Microsoft attributed a recent ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise to the China-aligned actor Storm-0940, which used the ARTEX agentic AI penetration-testing framework during the incident.
sections.why_it_matters: The event combines a software supply-chain compromise with automated offensive tooling.
sections.recommended_attention: Review ConnectWise Cloud Backup deployments, vendor advisories, and activity associated with affected systems.

stories.title: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching
stories.summary: CISA urged organizations to immediately patch CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws affecting PHP installations serving web requests. Fixed versions are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35.
stories.why_it_matters: An exploit attempt was detected before public disclosure, and unpatched internet-facing PHP systems are at risk.

stories.title: CISA: Hackers chain Plex flaws in Plex2Shell attacks to breach servers
stories.summary: CISA warned that attackers are actively exploiting four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server, collectively called Plex2Shell.
stories.why_it_matters: The flaws are being used to breach servers, making affected Plex deployments an immediate defensive priority.

stories.title: Critical GitLab Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Could Allow Unauthenticated RCE Across 12 Years of Releases
stories.summary: GitLab fixed a flaw allowing unauthenticated attackers to run code on self-managed servers. It affects versions dating back to 7.0, released in 2014, and an earlier update did not cover all affected releases.
stories.why_it_matters: The vulnerability's broad version range creates substantial exposure across long-lived self-managed GitLab installations.

stories.title: LiteLLM Compromised in Supply Chain Attack Delivering Credential Stealer and Backdoor
stories.summary: LiteLLM 1.107.0 was distributed through PyPI wheels and Docker images after attackers compromised multiple security controls. The release delivered a credential stealer and backdoor.
stories.why_it_matters: Software users may have imported malicious code into development, build, or production environments.

stories.title: Railway Says Intruder May Have Accessed Customer Secrets, Urges Credential Rotation
stories.summary: Railway disclosed anomalous activity involving systems that store customer environment variables. An unauthorized party may have accessed encrypted variables and, in some cases, decrypted contents.
stories.why_it_matters: Potentially exposed environment variables can provide access to applications, infrastructure, and other connected services.

stories.title: Node.js Brotli Decoder Bug Could Allow Remote Code Execution in All Supported Versions
stories.summary: Node.js released security updates for supported 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x lines, fixing 10 flaws. The most serious is a Brotli decompression bug that could allow remote code execution.
stories.why_it_matters: The flaw affects every supported Node.js release line and could enable attackers to run code on vulnerable systems.

stories.title: New QPACK Flaws Can Crash HTTP/3 Servers, Trigger Up to 4,000-Fold Memory Amplification
stories.summary: Unauthenticated attackers can send compressed HTTP headers that expand dramatically in memory, potentially crashing HTTP/3 servers. Working proof-of-concept code was released.
stories.why_it_matters: A small request volume could cause severe resource exhaustion and service disruption.

stories.title: Japan's Onamae Desktop Cloud hacked, up to 27,000 servers affected
stories.summary: Hackers compromised Onamae Desktop Cloud infrastructure and installed malware on as many as 26,739 customer servers.
stories.why_it_matters: The provider-level intrusion potentially affected thousands of downstream customer environments.

stories.title: CISA: SafePay ransomware hit over 600 critical infrastructure orgs
stories.summary: CISA said the SafePay ransomware group has breached more than 600 critical-infrastructure organizations worldwide since 2024.
stories.why_it_matters: The sustained campaign presents a significant risk to essential services and critical infrastructure operators.

stories.title: Eight eMudhra CA Keys Compromised, Triggering Emergency Fixes Across Browsers and Software
stories.summary: Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority certificates were compromised. Mozilla and Google's Chrome Root Program confirmed the issue, and browsers and software blocked the certificates.
stories.why_it_matters: The keys could have enabled forged trusted certificates for legitimate websites.

stories.title: China-Linked Hackers Use ARTEX AI Agents in ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
stories.summary: Microsoft said the China-aligned actor Storm-0940 was behind a recent ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise and used the ARTEX agentic AI penetration-testing framework during the incident.
stories.why_it_matters: The incident highlights the combination of supplier compromise and automated offensive tooling.

tts.text: Here is your cybersecurity briefing. First, CISA is urging immediate patching of two critical PHP vulnerabilities, known as PHP2Shell. They allow unauthenticated remote code execution, and an exploit attempt was detected before public disclosure. Attackers are also actively exploiting Plex Media Server flaws, so exposed Plex systems deserve urgent attention. GitLab fixed a maximum-severity remote-code-execution flaw affecting releases going back to 2014. The software supply chain is another major concern: compromised LiteLLM version 1.107.0 delivered a credential stealer and backdoor through PyPI and Docker images. Railway also warned that customer environment variables may have been accessed, making credential rotation important. Node.js fixed a remote-code-execution flaw in its Brotli decoder, while new QPACK flaws threaten HTTP/3 availability through extreme memory amplification. Finally, a cloud-provider compromise affected up to 26,739 Onamae servers, SafePay ransomware has hit more than 600 critical-infrastructure organizations, and compromised eMudhra certificate keys triggered browser blocking. Prioritize patching, credential rotation, and investigation of affected environments.
